alignments.note: Connective δέ → sentence-initial *Now*.
ἐπί rendered *in*; the preposition governing the phrase takes the English preposition under rule 36.

Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 splits the unit, and rule 22's determiner clause lets the article bring *the things* with the head on the nominal word *things*, the participle keeping the relative clause.
Attributive participle recast as a finite relative clause; the relativizer and copula are helpers on the participle under rules 7, 9 and 32, headed on the lexical verb *saying*.

Anarthrous Κεφάλαιον with a supplied *the* (rule 51's anarthrous clause, the determiner a rule 7 helper on the noun). Rule 66 heads on *point*, the noun glossing the lexeme, *chief* being the modifier.

Both words italicized in the ASV. *this* is a supplied cataphoric predicate answering to no source token at all, and rule 53 puts the supplied copula with the predicate, so the pair is `added` under rule 5. Folding *is this* onto Κεφάλαιον under rule 68 remains defensible, since that clause has no other token; I took `added` because rule 68 speaks of a supplied *subject* where none is expressed, and here the subject is expressed.
Inflected verb with its English subject; rule 9 heads on the lexical verb *have*.
Attributive demonstrative τοιοῦτον → *such*.
Anarthrous ἀρχιερέα with a supplied *a* (rule 51's anarthrous clause; rule 58 puts a phrase determiner on the noun). Rule 66 names ἀρχιερεύς → *high priest* headed on *priest*.
Relative pronoun → *who*.
καθίζω → *sat down*; *down* is the verb's own particle.
ἐν → *on*.
Substantival δεξιᾷ takes its own supplied determiner under rule 58, and rule 17's generic-noun clause heads on the adjective *right* rather than the supplied *hand*.
Rule 21: the article carries the case preposition, *of the* headed on *the*.
θρόνου → *throne*, standing alone under rule 21.
Rule 21 again: *of the* on the article.
μεγαλωσύνης → *Majesty*.
ἐν → *in*.
Rule 19: article → *the*.
οὐρανοῖς → *heavens*.

review_notes: The one contested unit is the italicized *is this*: taken as `added` because Κεφάλαιον is an expressed subject, so rule 68's no-subject configuration does not apply.
τοῖς λεγομένοις split under rule 32 rather than bundled, the article keeping *the things* and the participle the supplied relative clause.
